rationale: The assistant landed squarely on the hidden truth: clean the filter, clear and free the upper spray arm, top up salt, and run a longer/hotter normal programme rather than a short one, with no parts or engineer suggested. It used the customer's actual findings (food/grease in filter, stiff upper arm, seeds and limescale in holes, musty smell, top-rack-only grit) without inventing anything, and hedged appropriately. Weaknesses are a very long checklist-style first reply for a shorthand-typing homeowner, no direct question about which programme or whether salt had ever been filled, and the hot-cycle/door-seal/door-ajar advice repeated across all three replies, though not in a way that blocked progress.
